sources.title: Data Sources
questions: Primary data is User-Generated Video Content, which are sourced from the public, notable LGBTQ members and allies.As the videos contain the image and likeness, as well as narratives detailing their sexual identities, the data technically falls under GDPR’s Special Category Data that requires explicit consent to process (which the contributors have given by sharing their videos to Savage and Miller).
Another data source in the case study is Youtube’s metadata (e.g. the channels’ creation date), which is considered as sensitive engineering data and falls under proprietary laws.
For the videos, proper handling and processing on its intended purpose (i.e. sharing their stories) is crucial to ensure that IGBP complies with the Special Category Data statutes.
For Youtube’s metadata, strict engineering standards should be set to protect its quality and consistency and to avoid system errors based on corrupted data.

limitations.title: Limitations in data sources
questions: The primary limitations are: Youtube’s engineering lapses that allowed Chen to bypass protocol and alter production data. Youtube as a platform being context-blind, in the sense that it is optimized to uniformly treat channels the same.

On IGBP’s side, Savage loosened the curation process in favor of a seemingly first-in, first-out system within that 2-week period. This unknowingly implied a queue-like system where the sole arbiter for a video to be uploaded was that it was submitted earlier than others.

Youtube should improve their change management practices and introduce programs to aid the growth of socially-beneficial channels. IGBP should explore other sharing sites to upload videos and use cross-referencing between platforms.

sharing.title: Sharing data with others
questions: In the context of IGBP, the videos sent fall under Special Category Data. Thus it is not advisable to share them with others without the video sender’s explicit consent, despite the videos being publicly accessible in Youtube.
Given its proprietary nature, Youtube will not share its data to other organizations.

As the case study is more on the ethics of Chen’s actions rather than privacy issues, the mentioned parties should uphold the status quo while also being wary of the vulnerabilities that have been exposed through Chen’s actions.

ethical-legislative.title: Ethical and legislative context
questions: To address the ethics of Chen’s actions, we use the Kantian ethics, utilitarianism, and ACM’s code of ethics. To discuss Youtube’s inaction and context-blindness, we use care ethics and social justice, corporate social responsibility (CSR), Yogyakarta principles, and Floridi’s Information Ethics.
Legal frameworks that can be applied to Chen’s unauthorized production database changes are US Code 1030(5)(a), as well as GDPR’s Article 32.
As there was no adjudication for Chen’s actions, these ethical and legal frameworks would serve as references in analyzing future similar actions and in helping the platform improve.

rights.title: Rights around data sources
questions: The videos posted by the IGBP are sourced from support organizations and primarily individuals who sent their videos via email.

It is already in the discretion of Savage and Miller to curate the videos they receive so it will be amplified from a centralized platform of support to LGBT+ individuals. However the submitted videos remain to be under the property of IGBP, and so the use of the videos will legally be of the discretion of IGBP alone.

It must be covered under the terms of use the rightful use of the videos submitted to IGBP. It should also cover the ways in which users can request the removal of their videos from their platforms to accommodate the sense of control and trust of their supporters.

reasons.title: Your reasons for using data
questions: This multi-faceted data will be used to train the SuperFly model that will generate bespoke and immersive VR travel experiences to the client. SuperFly’s business model heavily relies on booking sales for customers.
IGBP’s videos aim to spread LGBTQ survival stories and messages of hope to the at-risk LGBTQ youth. Youtube’s metadata is primarily used for record-keeping and analytics purposes.

IGBP’s videos are a societal net positive as these address the rising suicide cases among the LGBTQ youth. Youtube’s metadata solely benefits the platform, and thus results in the limitations discussed.

communicating.title: Communicating your purpose
questions: The intent behind IGBP, which is to save lives by sharing stories, has been clear since the channel’s creation. The channel name and the actual content of the videos also provide context clues on this. Given the popularity of the project as described in the case study, it seems like the message has been relayed well.

Given the case description, it seems like IGBP is aware of Youtube’s limitations. However, the platform has not provided more information on why such policies exist. There also seems to be less consultations between Youtube and the channels, notably on how the platform could help them more.

positive-effects.title: Positive effects on people
questions: LGBTQ youth struggling with bullying, harassment, and suicidal ideation are the primary beneficiaries of this project. The videos provide messages of hope, showing that life can improve beyond the difficulties of adolescence. Those questioning their sexual orientation or gender identity can see positive role models and diverse life paths, reducing feelings of isolation and hopelessness.

Current measurement relies heavily on view counts (50 million+ views) and anecdotal testimonials claiming videos saved lives, but lacks systematic empirical validation. Chen stated they had "solid evidence that these videos did save lives" without detailing the methodology.

negative-effects.title: Negative effects on people
questions: Video contributors face significant privacy risks - LGBTQ youth who share videos could be outed to unsupportive families or communities, face targeted harassment or doxxing, and may have videos remain online permanently affecting future employment or relationships. Video viewers, particularly vulnerable LGBTQ youth in crisis, may be triggered by content discussing suicide or self-harm.

The case study reveals significant gaps in risk communication. There's no evidence of an informed consent process for video contributors about privacy risks, no content warnings about potentially triggering material, and no communication to Chen's colleagues about database risks before implementation.

mitigations.title: Minimising negative impact
questions: For Chen's case, harm can be minimised when establishing clear ethical review processes for engineers making judgment calls. Create escalation pathways for urgent decisions that bypass normal procedures. Implement monitoring systems to detect unintended consequences quickly.

Technical safeguards should include thorough sandbox testing before production changes, incremental database changes rather than dramatic backdating of six years, real-time monitoring for cascading effects, documented rollback procedures, and mandatory peer review for any changes outside normal procedures. Privacy and security measures must include encrypted submission channels, age verification with parental consent for minors, and a commitment to not track vulnerable viewers consuming crisis-related content.

engaging.title: Engaging with people
questions: In the context of IGBP, interested groups and individuals sent their videos to Savage and Miller for them to post to the IGBP channel. However the issue is that the channel is inherently subject to Youtube’s TOS, which restricts it to a limited number of videos since the year the channel was created.

No formal channels for appealing existed during that time, and so Savage and Miller found it hard to reach out to Youtube. It was only through the intervention of Chen that the issue was resolved in a questionable manner.
YouTube should also establish a communication channel to its creators, given that Chen’s intervention was just through their personal interest rather than from their professional capacity

openness.title: Openness and transparency
questions: Given that the document exists, it seems like Youtube has allowed for some part of the case to the authors. However, they did not disclose what the specific metadata column name is, nor did they disclose the workaround that Chen used.
In sharing such details, the intent is no longer to give feedback on the event but rather as a postmortem to study and reflect on the case and what could be done should a similar event occur.

Youtube made a wise decision to only share the relevant details of the case, as disclosing the methodology may entail additional security vulnerabilities. Given that this canvas also discusses the case in the context of what has been shared, it is safe to publish for public usage.

implementation.title: Ongoing implementation
questions: For IGBP, they are still actively promoting their message on a larger scale through creating a website where they have total control over how many videos they can publish, and have expanded to other video streaming platforms like TikTok and Discord. They have also maintained an open communication channel via email for people to reach out should they have concerns.

For YouTube, the regulations of limited video uploads are still standing. This has been codified in their terms and conditions and their community guidelines. They also have a support page where users can forward their concerns within a reasonable amount of time. However the case of Chen is still an exception.

review.title: Reviews and iterations
questions: For IGBP, data ethics issues can be measured through the feedback that the system gets from the videos streamed through our video streaming platforms. As Savage and Miller continue to curate their video collections, they shall also bear the responsibility in making sure that these remain to be compliant with the terms of service of their platforms.

For YouTube, data ethics issues in the case of Chen’s actions shall be addressed internally that despite it not having any adverse effects to the channel or to the platform at large, it begs the question on the community guidelines and terms of service.
The responses to this Data Ethics Canvas shall be reviewed and updated by the independent ethics committee from IGBP and YouTube on a regular monthly basis to ensure that integrity is maintained.

actions.title: Your actions
questions: Chen shall face an investigation attended by ethics committees and Youtube’s policymakers to discuss legal repercussions and policy changes in policy stemming from Chen’s actions.

In the case of YouTube, the company shall hold an internal investigation to revisit engineering standards and mitigate risks such as Chen’s actions, as well as discuss CSR-based actions to help socially-beneficial channels such as IGBP.
It shall be made sure by the ethics committee to release the results of the investigation, and also of this Data Ethics Canvas, to the public as soon as the report is ready to publish.
